title: Top Two Products in Each Category
description: Rank the products of every category by revenue and keep the best two: the top-N-per-group pattern.
statement:
Revenue is `quantity * unit_price` summed over the items of `paid` and `shipped` orders. For each product category return its **two products with the most revenue**: `category`, `product` (the name), `revenue` (rounded to 2 places). A category with only one product that has sold shows just that one; products that never sold are not listed. If two products have the same revenue, the one whose name comes first ranks higher.

Order by `category`, then revenue from the highest.
variants: UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id IN (1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12)
hints: Two steps: revenue per product, then the position of each product within its category.
`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC, product)`, then keep `pos <= 2`.
The filter on `pos` must be outside the query that computes it: use a second CTE or a subquery.
solution:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT p.category, p.name AS product, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items AS i
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.id = i.order_id
  JOIN products AS p ON p.id = i.product_id
  WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'shipped')
  GROUP BY p.id, p.category, p.name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT category, product, revenue,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC, product) AS pos
  FROM sales
)
SELECT category, product, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE pos <= 2
ORDER BY category, revenue DESC, product;
explanation:
**The idea.** "Top N per group" is the most common window-function question. Aggregate to one row per product, number the products inside each category with `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC)`, and keep the rows numbered up to N. `ROW_NUMBER` (not `RANK`) is right when you want *exactly* N rows per group and have a rule for ties (the name, here).

**Why two CTEs.** The first one is a plain `GROUP BY`; the second adds the numbering. The filter on the number can only come after, because a window function cannot be used in `WHERE` of the same query.

**Usual mistakes.** `LIMIT 2` (cuts the whole result, not each group); `RANK` with ties (more than N rows); numbering before aggregating (rows of a product, not products).
